name: How do you make a tub-to-shower conversion safer and less slippery?

mainEntity.name: What features make a converted shower safer and less slippery for daily use?
mainEntity.text: What features make a converted shower safer and less slippery for daily use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safety should be built into the shower design from the beginning. The most effective upgrades are slip-resistant flooring, properly placed grab bars, a handheld showerhead, and an entry that is easy to step into. A low-threshold or curbless design can help, but only if the drainage and waterproofing are done correctly. Good lighting matters too, especially in smaller bathrooms or for older adults. A bench or built-in seat may also improve safety and comfort. Homeowners should avoid smooth, glossy floor finishes and cheap hardware that feels unstable. In a conversion project, it is smart to think beyond the shower itself and consider towel placement, storage, and how water will stay contained. The safest bathrooms are designed around daily use, not just appearance. A contractor with accessibility experience can help choose features that reduce fall risk without making the shower look clinical or overly institutional.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use slip-resistant flooring, grab bars, a handheld showerhead, good lighting, and a low or curbless entry if possible. Proper drainage is also important, because standing water increases slip risk and makes the shower harder to use safely.
